problemSection.headline: The grid is the bottleneck for climate progress

cards.title: Demand is outpacing capacity
cards.description: Data centres, electrification of transport, heat pumps, industrial reshoring — every wedge of decarbonisation lands on the grid. Capacity isn't keeping up.

cards.title: Operators are flying blind
cards.description: Most grid operators still react to load instead of predicting it. The data exists — the intelligence layer doesn't, yet. That gap is where capital can do its best work.

cards.title: AI is the wedge — but who do you back?
cards.description: Hundreds of startups claim to apply AI to energy. A handful are real. Knowing which is the difference between a thesis and a portfolio.

valueProposition.headline: Two hours, three perspectives, one coherent thesis
valueProposition.body:
This isn't a broadcast webinar. It's a working session for serious allocators. We'll walk through the macro framing of the AI-and-grid intersection, share the investment thesis Carbon Equity is acting on, dig into specific portfolio companies building the intelligence layer for energy, and open the floor to your questions in the second hour.

If you're evaluating climate tech as an asset class — or already allocating and want to sharpen the energy lens — this is built for you.

services.headline: What we'll cover, end to end

cards.title: 30 min — The macro framing
cards.description: Where the grid sits in the climate transition, what's actually new about the AI layer, and the specific gaps that create investable companies.

cards.title: 45 min — Three companies, one thesis
cards.description: Three real portfolio investments — what they do, why we backed them, what the round looked like, and where they fit in the broader thesis.

cards.title: 45 min — Open Q&A with the team
cards.description: Your questions, on the record. Bring the hard ones — due diligence, fund mechanics, allocation sizing, exit assumptions, fee structure — anything goes.

caseStudies.headline: Three portfolio companies we'll go deep on

items.title: Grid intelligence platform
items.description: Real-time forecasting and optimisation software deployed across European TSOs. We'll cover the round, the moat, and what made it a conviction investment.

items.title: Battery dispatch optimisation
items.description: Software that turns utility-scale battery assets into actively traded grid resources. We'll walk through the unit economics and the comparable exits.

items.question: Who is this session for?
items.answer: Family offices, HNW individuals, fund-of-funds, and institutional allocators who are evaluating climate tech as an asset class — or already allocating and want a sharper energy-sector lens. Operators and founders welcome too, though the framing is investor-first.

items.question: Is it free?
items.answer: Yes. Carbon Equity hosts these sessions a few times a year as part of how we share what we're seeing in the market. No fee, no upsell, no hidden gating.

items.question: Will there be a recording?
items.answer: Yes. Within 48 hours of the live session you'll get the full recording, the slide deck, and a one-page summary. Share freely with colleagues.

items.question: What language is the session in?
items.answer: English. Q&A in English. The follow-up materials are in English too.

items.question: Can I ask questions live?
items.answer: Yes — the second hour is open Q&A, unmoderated. We pick up the hardest questions first. If you'd rather submit anonymously, the registration form has a field for that.

items.question: Do I need to be an accredited investor?
items.answer: No — this informational session is open to anyone interested in climate tech investing. To actually invest in a Carbon Equity fund, the usual accreditation rules apply (we'll cover them in detail during the session for anyone interested).
